Blowdown period (exhaust lead)
in a two-stroke, the crank angle between the exhaust port opening and the transfer ports opening, during which cylinder pressure falls below crankcase pressure.
Boost port
a transfer port opposite the exhaust port that sends charge up the rear cylinder wall, filling the region the main transfer streams leave stagnant.
Bore/stroke ratio
bore divided by stroke; above 1 is over-square (short stroke), below 1 is under-square (long stroke).
Brake thermal efficiency
brake power divided by the rate of chemical energy supplied in the fuel; about 28–32 % at best in a small air-cooled petrol engine.
Cam chain tensioner
spring-loaded ratchet or wedge plunger that presses a slipper blade against the cam chain to take up slack; automatic types can advance but not retreat.
Centrifugal oil filter
a rotor on the crankshaft of CG-type engines that spins sludge to its outer wall and must be opened and cleaned at service.
Collets (cotters)
two split tapered pieces that lock the valve spring retainer into a groove near the tip of the valve stem.
Crossplane crankshaft
inline-four crankshaft with crankpins at 90° intervals, which cancels inertial torque fluctuations and gives uneven firing intervals.
Delivery ratio
two-stroke equivalent of volumetric efficiency, based on one induction per revolution.
Effective (dynamic) compression ratio
compression ratio counted from the point where the inlet valve (four-stroke) or exhaust port (two-stroke) actually closes, lower than the geometric ratio.
Keystone ring
piston ring of tapered section, common in two-strokes, that flexes in its groove and resists sticking with carbon.
Leakage percentage
in a leak-down test, the fall from input pressure to cylinder pressure as a percentage of input pressure.
Lobe centre
crank angle at which a cam lobe gives maximum valve lift, used to check that a camshaft is correctly timed.
Napier ring
second compression ring with a hooked lower edge that scrapes oil downward; fitted with the notch pointing down.
Over-square
engine whose bore is larger than its stroke, favouring high rpm.
Plug chop
stopping the engine under load to read the spark plug for the combustion at that load, free of idling soot.
Pressed-up crankshaft
built-up crankshaft of two flywheel webs joined by a pressed-in crankpin, used with one-piece rods and roller big ends.
Pressure cap
radiator or header tank cap that holds the cooling system at typically 0.9–1.4 bar above atmospheric, raising the coolant boiling point.
Pumping work
work the piston spends drawing charge in and pushing exhaust out, greatest at part throttle where it works against manifold vacuum.
Residual gas
burnt gas left in the clearance volume at the end of the exhaust stroke, typically 5–15 % of the charge.
Ring end gap
gap between the ends of a piston ring fitted in the bore, allowing for thermal expansion; measured with feeler gauges.
Rotary (disc) valve
two-stroke inlet valve formed by a disc with a cut-out sector on the crankshaft, giving fixed asymmetric inlet timing.
Secondary inertia force
reciprocating force at twice crank frequency, about r/l of the primary force, caused by the finite length of the connecting rod.
Short-circuiting
loss of fresh two-stroke charge straight from the transfer ports out of the exhaust port during scavenging.
Stoichiometric ratio
chemically correct air-fuel ratio for complete combustion, about 14.7:1 by mass for petrol.
Thermostat
wax-element valve that keeps coolant in the engine until about 80–85 °C, then opens progressively to the radiator.
Trochoid pump
oil pump with an inner rotor having one lobe fewer than the outer rotor, so the chambers between them pump oil as they turn.
Under-square
engine whose stroke is longer than its bore, favouring low-speed torque.
Valve duration
crank angle during which a valve is open, for the inlet IVO + 180° + IVC.
Valve seat
hard ring of sintered iron or bronze alloy shrunk into the head, with a 45° sealing face on which the valve closes.
Valve stem seal
seal on top of the valve guide that meters oil to the stem and stops vacuum drawing oil down the inlet guide.
Wet compression test
compression test repeated with about 5 mL of oil in the cylinder; a large rise points to rings, piston or bore rather than valves.
